analysis: What changed vs the 7 AM brief: the slide deepened in the first 90 minutes — Nasdaq went from -1.2% to -1.8%, the S&P hit a 6.5-month low and the Nasdaq 100 a 7-month low, and the S&P broke below its 200-day moving average on Thursday, so this is now a seventh straight down day with the index under a widely watched trend line. Nvidia is the new leg down: -6.4% to ~$136.64, well below its $145.71 52-week low, with the whole chip complex (SMH -6%, AMD/MU/MRVL -6%, SNDK -7%) following it. Anthropic slid to ~$86.91, -10.6% on the day and only ~$4 above its $83 IPO price — the 'IPO as top' read is hardening by the hour. The one piece of genuinely dovish data, Michigan's final sentiment, barely registered: headline 51.5 matched estimates, but 1-year inflation expectations plunged to 3.7% from 4.7% and 5-year to 3.3% — the kind of print that would normally soften hike pricing, yet December hike odds sit at 96% and the tape ignored it. The Dow is the tell on rotation: +0.4-0.5% while tech sinks, led by health insurers (HUM +5%, UNH +3% on TD Cowen upgrades) and defensive food names. Signal vs noise: the seventh-day slide, NVDA breaking its low, ANT approaching $83, and the S&P under its 200-day are signal; the Dow's green print is rotation, not strength; the Michigan inflation-expectations drop is signal for the Fed path even if the tape shrugged today. The close now hinges on whether ANT holds $83, whether the S&P holds Thursday's 7,173.63 intraday low, and whether monthly options expiration adds a final volatility burst.

headlines.headline: Selloff deepens into a seventh straight down day: S&P 500 -0.7%, Nasdaq Composite -1.8%, Dow +0.4% mid-morning (IBD, ~7:45 AM PT). The S&P fell to a 6.5-month low and the Nasdaq 100 to a 7-month low (Barchart); the S&P closed Thursday below its 200-day moving average. Indexes are on track for their worst week since early last year — S&P and Dow down ~5% on the week, Nasdaq down more than 6%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The slide is accelerating into the session rather than stabilizing — and the Dow's gain is rotation into defensives, not broad strength.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) down ~10.6% to ~$86.91 at 10:58 AM ET (Finnhub), with an intraday low of $85 — only about $4 above the $83 IPO price. It opened at $89.86 and peaked at $92.56 this morning after closing Thursday at $97.17, down from its $111.50 debut open.
headlines.why_it_matters: Day two is now testing the IPO price itself — a break of $83 hardens the 'IPO as top' read and removes the AI trade's last floor.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) down 6.4% to ~$136.64 at 10:56 AM ET (Finnhub), with an intraday low of $135.62 — well below Thursday's $145.71 52-week low. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) is down nearly 6%. The California AG subpoena over China chips and investor disclosures, plus succession uncertainty around former CEO Jensen Huang, remain the overhang; the record Q3 (EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B) is not stopping the slide.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI bellwether is making new lows on its seventh straight down day — the leadership stock of the whole AI trade is now ~38% below its October peak.

headlines.headline: University of Michigan final consumer sentiment for November: 51.5, matching estimates and up from the 51.0 preliminary and 48.0 in October. The market-relevant detail: 1-year inflation expectations plunged to 3.7% from 4.7% in October, and 5-year expectations eased to 3.3% from 3.5% (InvestingLive, Finimize, ZeroHedge).
headlines.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations falling this fast is the dovish signal the Fed watches — but the tape ignored it today, so it matters more for the December meeting path than for today's price action.

headlines.headline: Chip rout broadens: Sandisk -7%, Micron and Marvell -6%, AMD -6%, Applied Materials and ARM -5%, plus cloud names Applied Digital -7% and CoreWeave -5% (Barchart). Meta -3%, Amazon, Microsoft and Tesla also lower (Investopedia). Alphabet and Apple, green early, are the only Mag 7 names holding up so far.
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff is now a liquidation of the whole AI complex, not just Nvidia — breadth inside tech is uniformly red, which is what makes the tape hard to stabilize.

headlines.headline: Defensive rotation is the other side of the tape: health insurers rally after TD Cowen upgraded Humana and UnitedHealth to Buy — Humana +5%, UnitedHealth +3%, Molina, Elevance and Cigna +2% — and defensive food producers (General Mills +3%, Smucker, Kraft Heinz, McCormick +2%) lead gainers. Gap is +15% after better-than-expected Q3 revenue trends at Old Navy and Gap. (Barchart)
headlines.why_it_matters: Money is rotating, not just leaving — defensives and a few earnings winners are absorbing flows, which is why the Dow is green while the Nasdaq sinks.

headlines.headline: December Fed hike pricing sits at 96% for a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting (Barchart), slightly off the ~97-99% of this morning. The 10-year Treasury yield is down ~6 bps to 4.99% as safe-haven buying continues — its fourth straight daily decline from the 5.05% Thursday close. Fed Governor Cook speaks at 12:15 PM ET. Gold futures are down 3% to $3,575 an ounce, their lowest since September 2025; WTI crude is $82.65, down 0.7%; Bitcoin ~$61,800. (Investopedia, Barchart)
headlines.why_it_matters: Yields falling while hike odds stay near-certain is the tension in the tape — bonds are pricing safety, not a Fed pivot, and gold's 3% drop shows even havens are being sold for liquidity.

headlines.headline: Intuit (INTU) down another 5-6% in the morning session after Thursday's ~10% drop on the Mailchimp sale to Bending Spoons (~$3.68B, about a third of the ~$12B it paid in 2021) and a cut to full-year revenue guidance, despite beating on the top and bottom lines. (Barchart, IBD)
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is still punishing the guidance cut and the fire-sale exit — and reading it as AI disruption hitting conventional software, which feeds the broader software de-rating.
